look_here_first: CREW FIELD ID: First find a low mat of running stems. Look at nodes for opposite paired leaves, and follow the thin mostly leafless flower stalk back to a leaf axil. Its tiny white/lilac flowers cluster around a purplish button that elongates with age. Inspect 3–5 mature leaves: a blade commonly widest beyond midlength, with most teeth toward the tip and a narrowing, less-toothed base. Rooting at buried/contact nodes is typical but may be hidden. These characters support Phyla; they do NOT unambiguously separate traditional P. nodiflora from P. lanceolata or P. cuneifolia, which a 2025 revision combines.

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: GROUND LEVEL: creeping perennial, frequently forming interconnected mats; a growing point may root where it touches soil

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: NODE: paired opposite (decussate) leaves with little or no visible stalk; young stems can appear nearly four-sided

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: LEAF: generally spoon-shaped to elliptic; many mature blades broader beyond halfway and toothed mainly nearer tip; check several leaves because this varies

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: FLOWER: one slender, mostly naked stalk from a leaf axil, topped with a tight button/cylinder of minute white to lavender two-lipped flowers

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: FRUIT: an older head becomes elongated and scaly; individual dry fruits split into two tiny one-seeded mericarps, not usually visible without dissection

lookalikes.differences: The best leaf split: P. nodiflora is usually widest beyond the middle and its teeth are concentrated in the distal half; P. lanceolata is widest nearer the middle and the teeth extend farther down the blade. Wedgeleaf frogfruit has a more distinctly wedge-shaped leaf architecture. Use several mature leaves rather than one odd leaf, because Phyla leaf shape varies along a shoot. Glandularia can also form low mats with verbena-like flowers, but its flowers are much larger and borne in more open terminal heads/spikes; Phyla has tiny flowers packed into a compact button/cylinder on a naked axillary peduncle.
